record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: When all jobs are present at time 0 and share a common speedup function that is neither of the form s(k)=k^p nor a simple threshold-based speedup function, what is the optimal way to allocate the n servers across jobs to minimize mean response time or mean slowdown?

evidence.quote: However if the speedup function is any non-trivial function other than s(k) = k^p or the simple threshold-based function, then it is an entirely open problem to determine how to optimally allocate servers to jobs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a system with $n$ identical servers and $m$ jobs, all present at time $0$. Each job has an inherent (sequential) size $X_i>0$. There is a common speedup function $s:\{1,2,\dots,n\}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ with $s(1)=1$ that is the same for every job: if a job is currently allocated $k$ servers, its remaining size decreases at rate $s(k)$. A scheduling policy is a (possibly time-varying) assignment of nonnegative integers $k_1(t),\dots,k_m(t)$ to the alive jobs at each time $t\ge 0$, subject to $\sum_i k_i(t)\le n$. Let $T_i$ denote the completion time of job $i$ under a given policy. Define the mean response time $\overline{T}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m T_i$ and the mean slowdown $\overline{S}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m T_i/X_i$.

Known special cases. When $s(k)=k^p$ for some $p\in(0,1]$, and when $s$ is a "threshold" speedup of the form $s(k)=k$ for $k\le k^\ast$ and $s(k)=s(k^\ast)$ for $k\ge k^\ast$, optimal allocation policies minimizing $\overline{T}$ (and $\overline{S}$) are known explicitly.

Problem. For an arbitrary speedup function $s$ that is neither a power law $s(k)=k^p$ nor a threshold function of the above form, determine the policy that allocates the $n$ servers to the $m$ jobs over time so as to minimize the mean response time $\overline{T}$, and separately the policy minimizing the mean slowdown $\overline{S}$, given that all jobs are present at time $0$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (heSRPT and follow-ups) explicitly solves the cases $s(k)=k^p$ and threshold speedups, and recent papers on the Core Allocation to Malleable jobs problem state that, for general concave speedup functions, optimizing mean response time with known job sizes "is still largely an open problem." No general solution for arbitrary speedup functions appears to be known.

status_evidence.title: heSRPT: Parallel scheduling to minimize mean slowdown
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal policy derived specifically for speedup s(k)=k^p.
status_evidence.claim: Optimal allocation is known for power-law speedup, motivating the open status for other speedup classes.

status_evidence.title: Mean field optimal Core Allocation across Malleable jobs
status_evidence.snippet: Prior work on the CAM problem has been largely limited to only one speedup function or a narrow class of speedup functions; optimizing mean response time is still largely an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: General speedup-function allocation for minimizing mean response time remains open.
